canonical.title: Kth element of two sorted arrays

narrative.title: Picking the k-th Batch from Two Interleaved Lines
narrative.scenario: Two production lines finish batches in individually sorted priority order, and dispatch needs the batch that would land in position k if both lines were merged. Merging kilobytes of batches just to read one position is wasteful, so the pick is made by cutting both lines at complementary points.
narrative.inputFormat: Two sorted arrays arr1 and arr2 of sizes N and M, and an integer K (1-based position in the merged order).
narrative.outputFormat: The element that would occupy position K in the sorted merge of arr1 and arr2.
constraints: An O(log(min(N, M))) algorithm is required

testCases.explanation: The merged order is 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and the fifth batch is 6.
Six batches precede 256 in the merged order, so it lands at position 7.

hintLevels: Level 1: The median solution generalizes - the median is just the special case where k is half the total.
Level 2: Search how many of the k elements come from the smaller array; the rest must come from the other, and validity is the same cross comparison of cut neighbours.

Level 3: The cut bounds must respect both arrays' sizes (a cut can neither reach past k nor leave the other array short), and the answer is the larger of the two left-cut values once the split is valid.
